description: One inbound tender: money moving from a payer to the merchant. Carries NO invoice linkage -- the invoice owns that relation via its own settlements[] array, so this schema says nothing about which invoice(s), if any, a payment applies to. This makes payment standalone-usable for donations, account top-ups, and prepayments that have no invoice at all, and lets one payment be split across multiple invoices without this schema needing to model the split -- the invoice-side settlement entry carries the applied portion.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- a value held under a property literally named payment is unambiguously a payment without needing $kind. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

amount.description: The amount of this inbound tender. Money returned is modeled as a separate billing.refund, never as a negative payment -- direction is carried by which schema you're looking at, not the sign of amount. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

customerId.description: Opaque id of the customer this payment is attributed to, keyed in the consumer's own system. Optional -- some payments (anonymous, gift, one-off top-ups) have no associated customer.

externalReferences.description: Links to corresponding records in foreign systems, e.g. Stripe or Shopify -- see external-reference for shape and validation. Replaces ad-hoc *Id fields scattered across schemas with one uniform array. A payment's externalReferences typically carries the processor's charge or PaymentIntent id.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

method.description: Open-vocabulary payment method, e.g. "card" or "bank_transfer". Not a closed enum -- new payment rails and processor-specific methods appear faster than a schema revision cycle would keep up with.

occurredAt.description: When this payment occurred (or was recorded), RFC 3339.

status.description: Current state of this payment attempt. Required, unlike the absent-means-default pattern used for catalog/document statuses elsewhere in this catalog -- a money-movement record's state is a fact its producer already knows at write time, and no default here is safe: defaulting an in-flight payment to succeeded would corrupt settlement math (amountPaid, amountDue) the moment it's referenced from an invoice's settlements[].
